finding.claim: Broken authorization on DELETE /projects/:id. The boolean result of authorized() is discarded, so the ownership/admin check is never enforced. Any authenticated user can delete any project.
finding.source: Authenticated non-owner, non-admin user sends DELETE /projects/:id with another user's project id (req.params.id)

trace.note: project fetched by attacker-controlled id with no ownership scoping
authorized() returns false for a non-owner, but the return value is ignored and it does not throw
authorized() only returns a boolean; unlike authorize() at line 4 it never throws

finding.guards_checked: The only check is the authorized() call, which is a no-op because its result is unused. The route has no other middleware in this file. Authentication is assumed to be set up elsewhere (req.user), but nothing here enforces per-resource authorization. The sibling PUT route correctly uses the throwing authorize().

verdict.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:18 only returns a boolean (api.js:12-14) and the result is discarded; no other middleware or check in this file. The throwing authorize() is used only on the PUT route (api.js:25).
verdict.reason: api.js:18 calls the non-throwing authorized() as a bare statement, so api.js:19 deletes the project for any authenticated user, owner or not. Authentication is assumed to be set up elsewhere, and a non-admin, non-owner is not meant to have this power.
